newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: PRESS DIGEST - Slovakia - Sept 23. [CORRECTED 11:10 GMT]
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Slovakia - Sept 23. [CORRECTED 11:10 GMT]

text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Slovak Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar has rejected an OECD opinion that Slovakia's microeconomic situation was not as good as the macroeconomic sphere.

- Meciar said the government intends to reduce unemployment to under 10 percent by the year 1998 from the current rate year-on-year rate of around 13 percent, (corrects economic indicator to unemployment from "inflation")

- Pavel Vana, administrator of the troubled Czech bank Ekoagrobanka appointed by the Czech National Bank, has critised the Slovak central bank's decision to withdraw the licence of the its Slovak branch, saying the move was groundless.
- The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) spokesman Jan Onda said an unspecified bank has expressed interest in buying the Ekoagrobanka's Slovak network.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Omnia, one of Slovakia's major export-import companies specialising mainly in trade with engineering products, posted turnover of more than three billion crowns in 1995, still far below the trunover of seven billion posted before the fall of communism in 1989.
PRAVDA - By the end of this year, Slovakia will prepare a law banning "excessive" imports, a law on the protection of imports at dumping prices and against imports of subsidised products.
- U.S. Defence Minister William Perry said Slovakia may be accepted into NATO "some time later" after the integration of the Czech Republic, Poland and Hungary.
- Holiday Inn will open it first hotel in Slovakia, in the capital Bratislava, on October 4.
